import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 3.5

by N. R. Brumberg

Can a subgroup of a relatively free group be radicable? In particular, can a verbal
subgroup of a relatively free group be radicable?

A group $F$ is *relatively free* if it is a free group of some variety of groups.
Equivalently (H. Neumann, *Varieties of Groups*, 1967), $F$ has a generating set $X$ such
that every map $X \to F$ extends to an endomorphism of $F$. We use the latter
characterization as the definition.

A group $H$ is *radicable* if every $h \in H$ has an $n$-th root in $H$ for every integer
$n \geq 1$. This is Mathlib's `RootableBy H ℕ`.

The *verbal subgroup* $W(F)$ of a group $F$ determined by a set of words $W$ (elements of the
free group on countably many variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$) is the subgroup generated by all
values $w(g_0, g_1, \dots)$ with $w \in W$ and $g_i \in F$. A subgroup is *verbal* if it is
of this form.

The trivial subgroup is verbal and radicable, so both questions ask for a *nontrivial*
radicable subgroup.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/
namespace Kourovka.«3.5»
variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

blocks.docstring:
A group `F` is *relatively free* if it has a generating set `X` such that every map
`X → F` extends to an endomorphism of `F`. Equivalently, `F` is a free group of some variety
of groups.

justification.closest_existing_considered: IsFreeGroup / FreeGroup (only absolutely free groups; relatively free groups such as free abelian or free nilpotent groups are not covered). No 'variety of groups', 'law', or 'verbal subgroup' exists in Mathlib (checked via rg).
justification.name: Kourovka.«3.5».IsRelativelyFree
justification.why_needed: Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib have no notion of a variety of groups or of a relatively free group. Defined via the standard characterization (H. Neumann, Varieties of Groups): F has a generating set X (Subgroup.closure X = ⊤) such that every map X → F extends to an endomorphism F →* F. This is equivalent to F being free in some variety of groups (F is then free in var(F) on X; conversely, any relatively free group F satisfies this since F belongs to its own variety).

blocks.name: IsRelativelyFree
blocks.text:
/-- A group `F` is *relatively free* if it has a generating set `X` such that every map
`X → F` extends to an endomorphism of `F`. Equivalently, `F` is a free group of some variety
of groups. -/
def IsRelativelyFree (F : Type*) [Group F] : Prop :=
  ∃ X : Set F, Subgroup.closure X = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ f : X → F, ∃ φ : F →* F, ∀ x : X, φ x = f x

blocks.code:
def IsRadicable (H : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  ∀ h ∈ H, ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → ∃ x ∈ H, x ^ n = h
blocks.docstring:
A subgroup `H` of a group is *radicable* if for every `h ∈ H` and every positive integer
`n` there is `x ∈ H` with `x ^ n = h`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: RootableBy (↥H) ℕ (Mathlib.GroupTheory.Divisible) — equivalent; used in the API lemma.
justification.name: Kourovka.«3.5».IsRadicable
justification.why_needed: Radicable subgroup: ∀ h ∈ H, ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → ∃ x ∈ H, x ^ n = h. Mathlib's RootableBy is a data-carrying class with a degenerate n = 0 clause; a Prop-valued predicate on Subgroup is cleaner in the statement. The API lemma isRadicable_iff_nonempty_rootableBy proves IsRadicable H ↔ Nonempty (RootableBy H ℕ).

blocks.name: IsRadicable
blocks.text:
/-- A subgroup `H` of a group is *radicable* if for every `h ∈ H` and every positive integer
`n` there is `x ∈ H` with `x ^ n = h`. -/
def IsRadicable (H : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  ∀ h ∈ H, ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → ∃ x ∈ H, x ^ n = h

blocks.code:
def verbalSubgroup (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure {g | ∃ w ∈ W, ∃ φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, φ w = g}
blocks.docstring:
The *verbal subgroup* `W(G)` of a group `G` determined by a set of words `W`, i.e. of
elements of the free group on the countably many variables `x₀, x₁, …`: the subgroup of `G`
generated by all values `w(g₀, g₁, …)` of the words `w ∈ W` at elements `gᵢ ∈ G`, that is,
by all images `φ w` under homomorphisms `φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: commutator / Subgroup.commutator / lowerCentralSeries (special cases of verbal subgroups, but no general notion); Subgroup.normalClosure and Subgroup.closure (used as building block).
justification.name: Kourovka.«3.5».verbalSubgroup
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no verbal subgroups. Defined for a set of words W ⊆ FreeGroup ℕ as Subgroup.closure of all values φ w (w ∈ W, φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* F). API tests: verbalSubgroup_empty (= ⊥), verbalSubgroup_singleton_of (word x₀ gives ⊤), verbalSubgroup_commutator (word [x₀,x₁] gives the commutator subgroup), verbalSubgroup_map_le (fully invariant).

blocks.name: verbalSubgroup

blocks.code:
def IsVerbal (H : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  ∃ W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ), H = verbalSubgroup W G
blocks.docstring:
A subgroup `H` of `G` is *verbal* if it is the verbal subgroup `W(G)` determined by some
set of words `W`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: commutator G / Subgroup.commutator (only the single verbal subgroup for the word [x₀,x₁]); Subgroup.Normal / Subgroup.Characteristic (weaker properties, not the definition). Nothing for general words or fully invariant subgroups exists.
justification.name: Kourovka.«3.5».IsVerbal
justification.why_needed: Verbal subgroup: ∃ W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ), H = Subgroup.closure {g | ∃ w ∈ W, ∃ φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, φ w = g}, i.e. H is generated by all values of the words in W under all homomorphisms of the free group on countably many letters into G. No such notion exists in Mathlib or the repo.

blocks.name: IsVerbal
blocks.text:
/-- A subgroup `H` of `G` is *verbal* if it is the verbal subgroup `W(G)` determined by some
set of words `W`. -/
def IsVerbal (H : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  ∃ W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ), H = verbalSubgroup W G

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isRelativelyFree_freeGroup (α : Type*) : IsRelativelyFree (FreeGroup α) := by
  refine ⟨Set.range FreeGroup.of, FreeGroup.closure_range_of α, fun f => ?_⟩
  refine ⟨FreeGroup.lift fun a => f ⟨FreeGroup.of a, a, rfl⟩, ?_⟩
  rintro ⟨_, a, rfl⟩
  simp
blocks.name: isRelativelyFree_freeGroup
blocks.text:
/-- Free groups are relatively free. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isRelativelyFree_freeGroup (α : Type*) : IsRelativelyFree (FreeGroup α) := by
  refine ⟨Set.range FreeGroup.of, FreeGroup.closure_range_of α, fun f => ?_⟩
  refine ⟨FreeGroup.lift fun a => f ⟨FreeGroup.of a, a, rfl⟩, ?_⟩

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isRadicable_iff_nonempty_rootableBy (H : Subgroup G) :
    IsRadicable H ↔ Nonempty (RootableBy H ℕ) := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    refine ⟨rootableByOfPowLeftSurj H ℕ fun {n} hn ⟨y, hy⟩ => ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨x, hx, hxy⟩ := h y hy n (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hn)
    exact ⟨⟨x, hx⟩, Subtype.ext hxy⟩
  · rintro ⟨_⟩ y hy n hn
    obtain ⟨⟨x, hx⟩, hxy⟩ := pow_left_surj_of_rootableBy H ℕ hn.ne' ⟨y, hy⟩
    exact ⟨x, hx, congrArg Subtype.val hxy⟩
blocks.docstring:
A subgroup is radicable in the sense of `IsRadicable` if and only if it is rootable by `ℕ`
in the sense of Mathlib's `RootableBy`.
blocks.name: isRadicable_iff_nonempty_rootableBy
blocks.text:
/-- A subgroup is radicable in the sense of `IsRadicable` if and only if it is rootable by `ℕ`
in the sense of Mathlib's `RootableBy`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isRadicable_iff_nonempty_rootableBy (H : Subgroup G) :
    IsRadicable H ↔ Nonempty (RootableBy H ℕ) := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    refine ⟨rootableByOfPowLeftSurj H ℕ fun {n} hn ⟨y, hy⟩ => ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨x, hx, hxy⟩ := h y hy n (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hn)
    exact ⟨⟨x, hx⟩, Subtype.ext hxy⟩
  · rintro ⟨_⟩ y hy n hn
    obtain ⟨⟨x, hx⟩, hxy⟩ := pow_left_surj_of_rootableBy H ℕ hn.ne' ⟨y, hy⟩
    exact ⟨x, hx, congrArg Subtype.val hxy⟩

theorem isRadicable_bot : IsRadicable (⊥ : Subgroup G) := by
  intro h hh n _
  exact ⟨1, one_mem _, by simpa using (Subgroup.mem_bot.mp hh).symm⟩

theorem verbalSubgroup_singleton_of : verbalSubgroup {FreeGroup.of 0} G = ⊤ := by

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_commutator :
    verbalSubgroup {⁅FreeGroup.of 0, FreeGroup.of 1⁆} G = commutator G := by
  rw [commutator_eq_closure, verbalSubgroup]
  congr 1
  ext g
  rw [mem_commutatorSet_iff]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨_, rfl, φ, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨φ (FreeGroup.of 0), φ (FreeGroup.of 1), (map_commutatorElement φ _ _).symm⟩
  · rintro ⟨a, b, rfl⟩
    refine ⟨⁅FreeGroup.of 0, FreeGroup.of 1⁆, rfl,
      FreeGroup.lift fun n => if n = 0 then a else b, ?_⟩
    rw [map_commutatorElement]
    simp
blocks.docstring: The verbal subgroup of the commutator word `[x₀, x₁]` is the commutator subgroup.
blocks.name: verbalSubgroup_commutator
blocks.text:
/-- The verbal subgroup of the commutator word `[x₀, x₁]` is the commutator subgroup. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_commutator :
    verbalSubgroup {⁅FreeGroup.of 0, FreeGroup.of 1⁆} G = commutator G := by
  rw [commutator_eq_closure, verbalSubgroup]
  congr 1
  ext g
  rw [mem_commutatorSet_iff]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨_, rfl, φ, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨φ (FreeGroup.of 0), φ (FreeGroup.of 1), (map_commutatorElement φ _ _).symm⟩
  · rintro ⟨a, b, rfl⟩
    refine ⟨⁅FreeGroup.of 0, FreeGroup.of 1⁆, rfl,
      FreeGroup.lift fun n => if n = 0 then a else b, ?_⟩
    rw [map_commutatorElement]
    simp

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_map_le (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (ψ : G →* G) :
    (verbalSubgroup W G).map ψ ≤ verbalSubgroup W G := by
  rw [Subgroup.map_le_iff_le_comap, verbalSubgroup, Subgroup.closure_le]
  rintro _ ⟨w, hw, φ, rfl⟩
  exact Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨w, hw, ψ.comp φ, rfl⟩
blocks.docstring: Verbal subgroups are fully invariant: every endomorphism maps them into themselves.
blocks.name: verbalSubgroup_map_le
blocks.text:
/-- Verbal subgroups are fully invariant: every endomorphism maps them into themselves. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_map_le (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (ψ : G →* G) :
    (verbalSubgroup W G).map ψ ≤ verbalSubgroup W G := by
  rw [Subgroup.map_le_iff_le_comap, verbalSubgroup, Subgroup.closure_le]
  rintro _ ⟨w, hw, φ, rfl⟩
  exact Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨w, hw, ψ.comp φ, rfl⟩

every $h \in H$ has an $n$-th root in $H$ for every integer $n \geq 1$? The subgroup is
required to be nontrivial because the trivial subgroup is radicable.

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no existence question: is there a variety of groups, a relatively free group F in it (equivalently, F has a generating set X such that every map X → F extends to an endomorphism of F), and a subgroup H ≤ F that is radicable (every h ∈ H has an n-th root in H for every integer n ≥ 1; cf. Mathlib `RootableBy H ℕ`, whose n = 0 case is degenerate); H must implicitly be required nontrivial (H ≠ ⊥), since the trivial subgroup is trivially radicable, and this automatically excludes the trivial variety and finite-exponent degenerate cases.
claims.reviewer_why: answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (F : Type) (_ : Group F), IsRelativelyFree F ∧ ∃ H : Subgroup F, H ≠ ⊥ ∧ IsRadicable H. Relative freeness via the (all-rank) equivalent endomorphism-extension characterization; radicability spelled out as n-th roots inside H for all n ≥ 1, with an API lemma proving equivalence to Mathlib's Nonempty (RootableBy H ℕ) (so the n = 0 clause of RootableBy is visibly harmless); H ≠ ⊥ excludes the trivially radicable trivial subgroup as the decomposition requires. c01/c04/c07 state the same proposition (c01/c07 via Nonempty (RootableBy H ℕ)); c02/c03/c05/c08 also faithful for this slot but were not chosen because their file's verbal slot uses full invariance. c06 chosen for its readable definitional style plus the RootableBy bridge lemma.

claims.decomposer_note: Subordinate special case of the primary question (flagged by 'In particular'; a positive answer here implies a positive answer above): the subgroup is additionally required to be verbal, i.e. generated by all values w(g₁,…,gₖ) of some set of words w (elements of a free group) under all homomorphisms into F (in a relatively free group these are exactly the fully invariant subgroups); again the verbal subgroup must be nontrivial, since the verbal subgroup of the identity word is ⊥ and trivially radicable.
claims.reviewer_why: Same as the primary slot with the extra conjunct IsVerbal H, where IsVerbal H := ∃ W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ), H = verbalSubgroup W F and verbalSubgroup W F is the subgroup generated by all images φ w (w ∈ W, φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* F) — the textbook word-value definition (Neumann's X_∞). I composed c06's IsVerbal with c01's reusable `verbalSubgroup` definition and its API/test lemmas (∅ ↦ ⊥, x₀ ↦ ⊤, [x₀,x₁] ↦ commutator subgroup, full invariance). c01/c04/c07 are equally faithful (c04 with an arbitrary alphabet). c02/c03/c05/c08 replaced 'verbal' by 'fully invariant'; that coincidence is a theorem only for relatively free groups of infinite rank and fails in general for finite rank, so those versions are a weakening of the source question and were rejected for this slot.

/-!
# Conjecture 3.5

by N. R. Brumberg

namespace Kourovka.«3.5»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A group `F` is *relatively free* if it has a generating set `X` such that every map
`X → F` extends to an endomorphism of `F`. Equivalently, `F` is a free group of some variety
of groups. -/
def IsRelativelyFree (F : Type*) [Group F] : Prop :=
  ∃ X : Set F, Subgroup.closure X = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ f : X → F, ∃ φ : F →* F, ∀ x : X, φ x = f x

/-- A subgroup `H` of a group is *radicable* if for every `h ∈ H` and every positive integer
`n` there is `x ∈ H` with `x ^ n = h`. -/
def IsRadicable (H : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  ∀ h ∈ H, ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → ∃ x ∈ H, x ^ n = h

/-- The *verbal subgroup* `W(G)` of a group `G` determined by a set of words `W`, i.e. of
elements of the free group on the countably many variables `x₀, x₁, …`: the subgroup of `G`
generated by all values `w(g₀, g₁, …)` of the words `w ∈ W` at elements `gᵢ ∈ G`, that is,
by all images `φ w` under homomorphisms `φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G`. -/
def verbalSubgroup (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure {g | ∃ w ∈ W, ∃ φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, φ w = g}

/-- A subgroup `H` of `G` is *verbal* if it is the verbal subgroup `W(G)` determined by some
set of words `W`. -/
def IsVerbal (H : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  ∃ W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ), H = verbalSubgroup W G

/-- Free groups are relatively free. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isRelativelyFree_freeGroup (α : Type*) : IsRelativelyFree (FreeGroup α) := by
  refine ⟨Set.range FreeGroup.of, FreeGroup.closure_range_of α, fun f => ?_⟩
  refine ⟨FreeGroup.lift fun a => f ⟨FreeGroup.of a, a, rfl⟩, ?_⟩
  rintro ⟨_, a, rfl⟩
  simp

/-- A subgroup is radicable in the sense of `IsRadicable` if and only if it is rootable by `ℕ`
in the sense of Mathlib's `RootableBy`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isRadicable_iff_nonempty_rootableBy (H : Subgroup G) :
    IsRadicable H ↔ Nonempty (RootableBy H ℕ) := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    refine ⟨rootableByOfPowLeftSurj H ℕ fun {n} hn ⟨y, hy⟩ => ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨x, hx, hxy⟩ := h y hy n (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hn)
    exact ⟨⟨x, hx⟩, Subtype.ext hxy⟩
  · rintro ⟨_⟩ y hy n hn
    obtain ⟨⟨x, hx⟩, hxy⟩ := pow_left_surj_of_rootableBy H ℕ hn.ne' ⟨y, hy⟩
    exact ⟨x, hx, congrArg Subtype.val hxy⟩

/-- The trivial subgroup is radicable. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isRadicable_bot : IsRadicable (⊥ : Subgroup G) := by
  intro h hh n _
  exact ⟨1, one_mem _, by simpa using (Subgroup.mem_bot.mp hh).symm⟩

/-- The verbal subgroup of the empty set of words is trivial. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_empty : verbalSubgroup ∅ G = ⊥ := by
  simp [verbalSubgroup]

/-- The verbal subgroup of the word `x₀` is the whole group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_singleton_of : verbalSubgroup {FreeGroup.of 0} G = ⊤ := by
  refine eq_top_iff.2 fun g _ => Subgroup.subset_closure ?_
  exact ⟨FreeGroup.of 0, rfl, FreeGroup.lift fun _ => g, by simp⟩

/-- The verbal subgroup of the commutator word `[x₀, x₁]` is the commutator subgroup. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_commutator :
    verbalSubgroup {⁅FreeGroup.of 0, FreeGroup.of 1⁆} G = commutator G := by
  rw [commutator_eq_closure, verbalSubgroup]
  congr 1
  ext g
  rw [mem_commutatorSet_iff]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨_, rfl, φ, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨φ (FreeGroup.of 0), φ (FreeGroup.of 1), (map_commutatorElement φ _ _).symm⟩
  · rintro ⟨a, b, rfl⟩
    refine ⟨⁅FreeGroup.of 0, FreeGroup.of 1⁆, rfl,
      FreeGroup.lift fun n => if n = 0 then a else b, ?_⟩
    rw [map_commutatorElement]
    simp

/-- Verbal subgroups are fully invariant: every endomorphism maps them into themselves. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_map_le (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (ψ : G →* G) :
    (verbalSubgroup W G).map ψ ≤ verbalSubgroup W G := by
  rw [Subgroup.map_le_iff_le_comap, verbalSubgroup, Subgroup.closure_le]
  rintro _ ⟨w, hw, φ, rfl⟩
  exact Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨w, hw, ψ.comp φ, rfl⟩

/-- The trivial subgroup is verbal. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isVerbal_bot : IsVerbal (⊥ : Subgroup G) :=
  ⟨∅, verbalSubgroup_empty.symm⟩

/--
Can a subgroup of a relatively free group be radicable?

That is, is there a relatively free group $F$ and a nontrivial subgroup $H \leq F$ such that
every $h \in H$ has an $n$-th root in $H$ for every integer $n \geq 1$? The subgroup is
required to be nontrivial because the trivial subgroup is radicable.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«3.5» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (F : Type) (_ : Group F), IsRelativelyFree F ∧
      ∃ H : Subgroup F, H ≠ ⊥ ∧ IsRadicable H := by
  sorry

/--
In particular, can a verbal subgroup of a relatively free group be radicable?

That is, is there a relatively free group $F$ and a nontrivial verbal subgroup $H \leq F$,
i.e. $H = W(F)$ for some set of words $W$, such that every $h \in H$ has an $n$-th root in
$H$ for every integer $n \geq 1$? The subgroup is required to be nontrivial because the
trivial subgroup (the verbal subgroup of the empty set of words) is radicable.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«3.5».variants.verbal_subgroup : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (F : Type) (_ : Group F), IsRelativelyFree F ∧
      ∃ H : Subgroup F, H ≠ ⊥ ∧ IsVerbal H ∧ IsRadicable H := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«3.5»

items: Relatively free is formalized by the endomorphism-extension characterization (generating set X such that every map X → F extends to an endomorphism), rather than by first defining varieties of groups; the two are equivalent (H. Neumann, Varieties of Groups, 1967).

Words for verbal subgroups are taken in FreeGroup ℕ (countably many variables), the textbook convention; since every word involves finitely many letters, this yields exactly the same verbal subgroups as words over an arbitrary alphabet.

Radicability requires n-th roots to lie in H itself (H is radicable as a group), for every positive integer n; n = 0 is excluded (Mathlib's RootableBy handles n = 0 by a degenerate clause; equivalence proved in an API lemma).

Both slots require H ≠ ⊥, following the decomposition table: the trivial subgroup is radicable and verbal, so without this the questions would be trivially answered 'yes'. No other restriction is added; e.g. finite-exponent varieties and free groups are automatically excluded by the mathematics rather than by hypotheses.
F is quantified over Type (universe 0), matching the convention of the other Kourovka files (∀/∃ (G : Type) [Group G]).

reviewer_notes: Both slots ship. Modeling decisions: (1) 'relatively free' = has a generating set X such that every map X → F extends to an endomorphism of F; this is equivalent to 'free in some variety' for all ranks (F is then free in var(F): the kernel of FreeGroup X → F consists exactly of X-laws of F). (2) 'radicable' = every element has an n-th root in H for every n ≥ 1, roots inside H (H radicable as a group); proven equivalent to Nonempty (RootableBy H ℕ). (3) 'verbal' by word values over FreeGroup ℕ, not via full invariance (the fully-invariant candidates c02, c03, c05, c08 rely on the infinite-rank theorem 'verbal = fully invariant', which is not valid for finite rank, so their variant slot is not a faithful rendering of 'verbal'). (4) Nontriviality H ≠ ⊥ is imposed in both slots, per the decomposition table, since ⊥ is verbal and radicable; no further restriction is needed (finite-exponent varieties and absolutely free groups are excluded by the mathematics, not by hypotheses). F is quantified over Type (universe 0), following the other Kourovka files. Bespoke definitions are kept in the problem file since a single output file was requested; a maintainer could move verbalSubgroup/IsRelativelyFree to FormalConjecturesForMathlib. Final file compiles with only 'declaration uses sorry' warnings.
